seo_title: Calcutta HC: Appeal Doesn't Automatically Stay Demolition
title: Calcutta High Court: A Pending Appeal Does Not Automatically Stay a Demolition Order
case_name: Dulal Chandra Sanfui v. Sub-Divisional Officer, Baruipur & Ors.
card_summary: The Calcutta High Court had already quashed a Baruipur owner's construction as illegal and ordered its demolition. When the Sub-Divisional Officer later issued a demolition directive, the owner filed a fresh writ, arguing his pending appeal kept the matter from becoming final. Justice Rishad Medora rejected this, holding a pending appeal does not by itself stay an order that has not been separately stayed.
card_tip: Filing an appeal against an adverse order does not pause its enforcement; a party seeking protection must apply for and obtain an actual stay, not rely on the appeal being pending.
verification_notes: The 9 November 2026 decision date, the presiding judge (Justice Rishad Medora), the petitioner's name and the Baruipur location are reported consistently across LiveLaw, LawChakra and SupremeToday. The background facts, the September 2026 quashing order and the October SDO demolition directive, are recited the same way in all three reports, though the exact dates in September and October differ slightly between sources, so the card states only the month, not the exact day, for those two steps. No WPA or case number for this specific writ was found in the sources opened in this run, so the citation field is left without one rather than guessed.
